accuracy.evidence: Checked against the British Antarctic Survey emperor penguin fact sheet (largest penguin, about 1.1-1.2 m; female lays one egg in May-June and passes it to the male, who incubates it on his feet under a brood pouch for about 64-67 days while fasting; female returns about hatching), Australian Antarctic Division pages on little penguins (about 30-33 cm) and Adelie penguins (about 70 cm), Gilbert et al. 2006 (huddle temperatures above 30 C, birds rotate between edge and centre), Wienecke et al. 2007 (emperor dives beyond 500 m) and BirdLife on African and Galapagos penguins (Galapagos penguins live on the equator, the only penguins that reach north of it). The lesson says 'almost all' live in the south half for that reason; 'some swim faster than you can run' rests on gentoo bursts of about 36 km/h.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets common children's ideas about penguins reported in Tunnicliffe and Reiss (1999) on how children classify animals and in RSPB and Natural History Museum teacher notes: birds must fly (prediction 1, 'fly' feedback, m1), penguins and polar bears share a home (p5, 'north'), all penguins live on ice (prediction 5, 'ice2', m5), the mother sits on the egg in a nest (prediction 3, 'nest', p3, m7), the egg can rest on the ice ('ice'), and only the big or strong birds get warm in a huddle (prediction 4, 'big').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpengu is about one animal group's own body and behaviour: a penguin that only hops when it flaps but zooms once dragged into the sea, four species stood in height order beside a 115 cm child, an egg dragged from mum's feet to dad's feet that is sent back if released over the ice, a 65-day winter counter while mum walks to the sea, a ten-bird huddle where tapping an edge bird swaps it with the warmest middle bird, and a five-species sort into icy and warm homes plotted on a north/south map. flagpolaran sorts many animals between the poles and has blubber, fox coats and a build-a-body blizzard; its huddle squeezes birds together, while this one is about rotation turns. Gate lab_distinct passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each fact is found by doing before the text states it: repeated flaps never lift the penguin but the dive shows the wings driving it underwater; standing the emperor last puts its head level with the 6-year-old; dropping the egg anywhere but dad's feet turns it blue and sends it back; the day counter climbs to 65 before the chick appears and mum returns; edge birds turn pale and blue-dotted until they are swapped in; the warm-home cards land as orange dots all below the equator.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes, all birds fly' (flapping fails), 'a cat' for the biggest penguin (the emperor matches the child), 'mum' keeping the egg (dad holds it while mum leaves), 'only the biggest ones' keeping warm (every bird must get a turn), and 'yes, all of them' living on ice (three of five species have warm homes).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with nine distinct feedback messages naming the slip: penguins cannot fly because their wings are flippers; little penguin 30 cm against emperor 115 cm; emperors make no nest; an egg on the ice would freeze; huddling is not a game; every bird takes a turn, big or small; no wild penguins near the North Pole; some live on warm beaches; wings are not useless because they drive swimming.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 1.8 in short sentences with the target words bird, flipper, emperor, huddle, egg, south; adult text stays within the 9.5 limit overall and lists key vocabulary and the Year 1 and Year 2 aims. Lab steps are one to three short sentences; species names are shortened to one word on buttons; sizes are compared with a child and a ruler rather than raw numbers alone; the young layout gives 56 px buttons.

no_filler.evidence: Gate finds no filler phrases. Each kid paragraph carries one theme (flying versus swimming, size, the egg, the huddle and where penguins live). Items are varied: p2 and m8 count penguins in a huddle, p4 compares little and emperor heights, m6 counts days left until hatching, p5 and m4 address where penguins live, and m9 checks what the mother does.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the penguin, egg and huddle birds are large drag or tap targets on the 390 px tall layout; height labels sit on white pills under each bird; the egg scene keeps mum, dad and the sea visible together; the map dots no longer cover the 'south half' label after moving the Adelie dot; controls are 56 px young buttons wrapping to two rows with nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: Flap and Dive in, a button per species for the height line, Pass egg to dad and Mum goes to sea, Let a cold one in, and Icy home or Warm home. The canvas aria-label is updated with each result (heights, days, huddle turns, homes), challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
